items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: He always was very supportive of me. And what I liked in his later years, which is what I was a part of is that he liked surrounding himself with younger players.

ctx.x: Speaking of liking people, did you enjoy your stint with Benny Goodman?

Yes. I had — well I mean we were treated like kings by the audiences I mean the thrill of my opening night, 18,000 people, I mean I was shaking so much that we played “Let’s Dance” and I’m [scats]. I mean literally I couldn’t stop shaking. And I had nothing but good experiences with Benny myself. He always was very supportive of me. And what I liked in his later years, which is what I was a part of is that he liked surrounding himself with younger players. It made him feel I think more vital. And it also provided…
There sure are a lot of places in the country now that you can go to study jazz.
